title: Agentic AI and the Deconstruction of White-Collar Labor Costs
summary: The transition from passive LLMs to autonomous AI agents marks the onset of the first true intellectual automation wave, directly threatening traditional white-collar roles in finance and corporate operations. In the short term, this technical shift allows corporations to slash operating expenses and run 24/7, driving profit margins and stock valuations higher. However, from a macroeconomic perspective, this rapid displacement risks breaking the circular flow of income and consumption, as the purchasing power of the professional class is eroded. For finance students like Jaehyuk Song, this highlights the critical need to transition corporate valuation models from tracking mere short-term productivity to evaluating systemic consumer demand sustainability.

title: Democratizing AI Wealth: Restructuring Asset Ownership to Prevent Demand Collapse
summary: As AI captures an unprecedented share of economic output, the concentration of capital among a handful of technology monopolies threatens to disrupt the circular economy by depressing aggregate consumer demand. To counteract this trend, financial markets and policymakers must pivot toward broader asset ownership models, such as sovereign wealth funds and AI-dividend ETFs that redistribute automation gains. By ensuring that the wealth created by intellectual automation circulates back to the public, society can sustain the consumer spending necessary to fuel corporate revenues. For future financial leaders, understanding these distributive mechanisms is no longer just an ethical consideration, but a fundamental requirement for maintaining long-term market stability.

title: Re-engineering Human Capital: Why AI Demands a Revolution in Educational Value
summary: The automation of cognitive labor renders traditional, memory-based business education obsolete, necessitating an immediate shift toward teaching problem-defining, leadership, and complex negotiation. As AI models increasingly handle routine quantitative analysis, the financial value of human capital will reside solely in high-level qualitative judgment and creative synthesis. Without systemic education reform, the labor market risks severe polarization, further choking the circular flow of economic value through rising unemployment. For business students, prioritizing these non-automatable leadership and decision-making skills is the ultimate hedge against intellectual obsolescence in a hyper-automated financial landscape.

title: The AI Capex Paradox: Boosting Corporate Margins at the Expense of the Consumer Engine
summary: As tech giants aggressively scale capital expenditure on AI infrastructure, financial markets are cheering short-term efficiency gains and skyrocketing corporate profit margins. However, this capital-intensive shift risks disrupting the fundamental circular flow of the economy by automating intellectual labor and reducing overall wage income. If widespread white-collar displacement erodes aggregate consumer purchasing power, the very corporations investing in AI will eventually face a severe demand deficit in consumer-facing sectors. Consequently, long-term asset valuation must discount this systemic risk unless productivity gains are redistributed to sustain consumer spending.

title: Concentrated Wealth Accumulation and the Strategic Necessity of Democratic Asset Ownership
summary: The modern stock market is experiencing historic levels of concentration as capital flows disproportionately to a handful of AI-pioneering mega-cap equities. Under our analytical framework, this concentration highlights a critical distribution problem: while AI-driven productivity gains are captured by a narrow group of shareholders, the broader labor force faces structural income stagnation. To prevent a systemic consumption collapse, financial institutions and policymakers must pioneer innovative retail investment vehicles, sovereign wealth funds, and pension models that democratize equity ownership. Without these mechanisms to distribute AI-driven wealth, the circular flow will fail, ultimately undermining the macroeconomic foundation that supports financial markets.
